history.new: Every structured quasigroup tested (affine, XOR, x + c(y), (x + 1) XOR y) gives a larger maximal avalanche bias than the random Latin square, in the reverse-pass (p2+rev) construction. (As first worded - 'in the same construction' - the hypothesis is false for the forward-only construction, where the random Latin square and x + c(y) both have bias exactly 1/2 by CLM-C18-02; the experiment compared every structured variant with QG-LS p2+rev.)
history.old: Every structured quasigroup tested (affine, XOR, x + c(y), (x + 1) XOR y) gives a larger maximal avalanche bias than the random Latin square in the same construction.
history.reason: Skeptic review 2026-10-18 (P8) - statement restricted to the reverse-pass construction actually tested

limitations: Proved (bias 1/2) for the T-function and GF(2)-affine quasigroups (CLM-C18-04, CLM-C18-05). For x + c(y) with a reverse pass the difference (0.043 versus 0.041) is within sampling noise; its defect shows in bit independence instead (CLM-C18-06), which the hypothesis did not measure.
statement: Every structured quasigroup tested (affine, XOR, x + c(y), (x + 1) XOR y) gives a larger maximal avalanche bias than the random Latin square, in the reverse-pass (p2+rev) construction. (As first worded - 'in the same construction' - the hypothesis is false for the forward-only construction, where the random Latin square and x + c(y) both have bias exactly 1/2 by CLM-C18-02; the experiment compared every structured variant with QG-LS p2+rev.)
title: H-C18-2: structured quasigroups are worse mixers than a random Latin square (maximal avalanche bias)
